Longevity and
Functional Medicine.

Root-cause investigation and the science of healthy ageing, for the years before illness declares itself. Harley Street, Wimbledon and online globally.

Book an AppointmentDiscover the service ↓
The service

What is longevity and functional medicine?

Conventional medicine is built around disease. It diagnoses conditions once they have declared themselves, and manages symptoms once they have taken hold. What it rarely has the time to address is the territory in between: the years, sometimes decades, during which the body is moving in the wrong direction without yet crossing a clinical threshold.

Functional medicine asks why a symptom has arisen rather than which drug will manage it, tracing the hormonal, metabolic, environmental and lifestyle factors driving it. Longevity medicine applies the same thinking across a longer horizon, using the current science of healthy ageing to slow what accelerates decline.

Here the two are inseparable: every longevity assessment carries the benefit of functional investigation, and every complex or chronic presentation is read through the lens of long-term resilience.

We see patients at our Harley Street clinic, our Wimbledon clinic, and via secure online consultations globally.

What it involves

Eleven strands of investigation, one plan.

Longevity and functional medicine draw on a wider range of testing than a standard consultation allows. Every strand below is used only where your presentation calls for it.

Longevity and functional medicine work demands time that standard appointments cannot provide. Your initial consultation with your doctor is a dedicated clinical conversation covering your full medical history, your current health concerns, your family history, your lifestyle, your goals, and any previous investigations or treatments you have undergone.

Where relevant, a pre-consultation blood panel is arranged in advance so that meaningful data is available from the outset. Depending on the depth of investigation required, additional functional testing is recommended following your first appointment.

Chronological age and biological age are not the same thing. Biological age, measured through epigenetic markers such as DNA methylation patterns, reflects the rate at which your cells and tissues are actually ageing. It is a more clinically meaningful indicator of long-term health risk and vitality than the number of years you have lived.

We use validated biological age testing to establish your current epigenetic age and to identify the lifestyle, nutritional, hormonal, and metabolic factors driving acceleration or deceleration of that process. This forms the foundation of a personalised longevity plan aimed at measurably slowing biological ageing over time.

A longevity assessment at The Schoeman Clinic is not a single test. It is a structured clinical process that draws together multiple streams of investigation: advanced blood biomarkers, hormonal panels, metabolic markers, cardiovascular risk assessment, gut health evaluation, epigenetic data, and a detailed clinical interview. The result is a comprehensive picture of your current health status, your risk trajectory, and the specific biological processes most in need of intervention.

Assessments are entirely personalised. No two patients receive the same protocol, because no two biological profiles are identical.

Your genes are not your destiny, but they do define your tendencies. Nutrigenomic testing analyses how your unique genetic variants influence your response to nutrition, your susceptibility to inflammation, your detoxification pathways, your cardiovascular risk, and your hormonal metabolism. This data allows us to move beyond generalised dietary advice and into genuinely personalised nutritional and supplemental prescribing that works with your biology rather than against it.

Epigenetic profiling goes a step further, examining how lifestyle, environment, and other factors are influencing which genes are expressed and which are suppressed. These patterns are modifiable, and understanding them is one of the most powerful tools available in longevity medicine.

Mitochondria are the energy-producing structures within every cell in the body. Their function declines with age and under conditions of chronic stress, poor nutrition, environmental toxin exposure, and hormonal imbalance. Impaired mitochondrial function underlies many of the most common complaints seen in functional medicine practice, including chronic fatigue, brain fog, poor exercise tolerance, and metabolic dysfunction.

We assess mitochondrial health through functional testing, including organic acids testing (OAT) where clinically indicated, and develop targeted programmes to restore cellular energy production through nutritional medicine, lifestyle intervention, and where appropriate, targeted supplementation.

Metabolic dysfunction is one of the most significant drivers of accelerated biological ageing, cardiovascular risk, hormonal imbalance, cognitive decline, and chronic disease. Insulin resistance, in particular, is frequently present for years or decades before it is formally identified, during which time it silently damages blood vessels, disrupts hormonal signalling, promotes inflammation, and impairs cognitive function.

We investigate metabolic health in depth, using fasting insulin, HbA1c, lipid subfractions, inflammatory markers, and hormonal assessment alongside your clinical presentation. Treatment is personalised and may include nutritional intervention, lifestyle medicine, targeted supplementation, and hormonal correction where appropriate.

The gut microbiome, the vast and dynamic ecosystem of microorganisms inhabiting the digestive tract, influences immune function, hormonal metabolism, inflammation, brain health, and metabolic regulation. Dysbiosis, an imbalance in microbial diversity and composition, has been linked to conditions ranging from irritable bowel syndrome and autoimmunity to depression, obesity, and accelerated ageing.

We assess gut health through advanced stool testing, including the GI360 comprehensive microbiome analysis available through our diagnostics service, and develop targeted restoration protocols based on your results.

Cognitive resilience, the capacity to maintain sharp thinking, clear memory, and emotional stability across a lifetime, is a central goal of longevity medicine. Brain health is not independent of body health. Hormonal balance, metabolic function, sleep quality, gut health, inflammatory load, and cardiovascular risk all exert measurable influence on cognitive performance and long-term neurological resilience.

We assess brain health as part of the broader longevity picture, identifying the biological factors most likely to be impeding cognitive performance or increasing long-term neurological risk, and developing a personalised plan to address them.

Chronic low-grade inflammation is a central mechanism in accelerated ageing and in the development of a wide range of conditions, from cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes to autoimmunity and neurodegenerative illness. Standard blood tests often miss subclinical inflammation, focusing on acute-phase markers rather than the more sensitive functional indicators that reflect chronic systemic burden.

We assess inflammatory status using a broader range of markers, including high-sensitivity CRP, homocysteine, ferritin, and other functional biomarkers, and investigate the drivers of inflammation through a root-cause lens that includes gut integrity, environmental toxin burden, hormonal imbalance, and dietary patterns.

Exposure to environmental chemicals, including heavy metals, pesticides, plasticisers, mycotoxins, and other persistent pollutants, is an underappreciated contributor to fatigue, hormonal disruption, neurological symptoms, and metabolic dysfunction. Cumulative toxic burden accumulates quietly over years, and standard investigations rarely assess it.

We offer environmental toxin testing through our diagnostics service, including mycotoxin testing and organic acids analysis, and develop personalised detoxification protocols to support the body’s clearance pathways.

Prevention is the most powerful medicine available. The interventions most likely to extend healthy lifespan, protect cognitive function, preserve cardiovascular health, and maintain hormonal vitality are not experimental. They are evidence-based, clinically validated, and available now.

At The Schoeman Clinic, we translate the current science of longevity into practical, personalised protocols that patients can implement in their daily lives. This includes cardiovascular risk reduction, hormonal optimisation, targeted nutritional prescribing, sleep medicine, stress resilience, and evidence-based supplementation, all coordinated within a coherent clinical plan rather than applied piecemeal.

Who this is for

Is this service right for you?

Longevity and functional medicine at The Schoeman Clinic is appropriate for adults who recognise themselves in the situations below.

  • Healthy, and looking ahead

    In good or reasonable health, but wanting to understand your biological age and optimise your long-term trajectory.

  • Complex, unexplained symptoms

    Living with complex, chronic or multi-system symptoms that have not been fully explained or resolved through conventional investigation.

  • Diagnosed, not resolved

    You have a diagnosis, but feel the underlying drivers of your condition have not been adequately addressed.

  • Midlife, taken seriously

    Approaching or navigating midlife and wanting an informed, proactive approach to healthy ageing.

  • Fatigue, fog, declining resilience

    Experiencing fatigue, brain fog, metabolic difficulties or declining resilience that you attribute, at least in part, to the ageing process.

  • Cutting-edge longevity science

    Wanting access to epigenetic profiling, biological age testing and personalised preventative protocols, delivered within a rigorous clinical framework.

This service is suitable for both women and men and is available to patients at all stages of adulthood.

Book an Appointment
The distinction

How functional medicine differs from conventional investigation.

Functional medicine does not replace conventional medicine. It extends it.

Where conventional assessment identifies the presence or absence of diagnosable disease, functional investigation explores the continuum of biological function that precedes disease, identifying patterns of dysfunction before they cross clinical thresholds and before they cause irreversible harm.

This means using a wider range of tests, applying different reference standards, taking a longer and more detailed clinical history, and spending considerably more time with each patient than a standard NHS or private GP appointment allows. It means viewing the body as an integrated system rather than a collection of independent organ systems, and recognising that symptoms in one area almost always have roots in processes occurring elsewhere.

The principle
“Medicine should protect health before disease takes hold, not simply manage it once it has.”
Dr Gina Schoeman · Founder & Medical Director
